refs.ieee: Y. Hu, Y. Koren, and C. Volinsky, "Collaborative filtering for implicit feedback datasets," in Proc. 8th IEEE Int. Conf. Data Mining (ICDM), Pisa, Italy, 2008, pp. 263–272, doi: 10.1109/ICDM.2008.22.
refs.topic: (a) Implicit-feedback matrix factorization (weighted ALS) on TV viewing data
refs.why_relevant: This is the core paper for the MF method. It treats implicit signals (the abstract names 'watching habits') as binary preference with varying confidence, and its optimization scales linearly with data size. The abstract says the algorithm 'is used successfully within a recommender system for television shows', which makes it the closest classical precedent for sweet.tv viewing logs. The docs of implicit's AlternatingLeastSquares (benfred.github.io/implicit/api/models/cpu/als.html) say the model is based on this paper.
refs.verified_via: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1109/ICDM.2008.22 gives the authors (Yifan Hu, Yehuda Koren, Chris Volinsky), the venue '2008 Eighth IEEE International Conference on Data Mining' (Pisa, Italy), pp. 263-272, Dec 2008, IEEE. OpenAlex W2101409192 has the same pages and the abstract. doi.org returns 302 to ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/4781121.

refs.ieee: S. Rendle, C. Freudenthaler, Z. Gantner, and L. Schmidt-Thieme, "BPR: Bayesian personalized ranking from implicit feedback," in Proc. 25th Conf. Uncertainty Artif. Intell. (UAI), Montreal, Canada, 2009, pp. 452–461. [Online]. Available: https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.2618

refs.why_relevant: BPR gives a pairwise ranking objective for implicit data, so it is a natural MF variant to compare with ALS under MAP@5. The docs of implicit's BayesianPersonalizedRanking say it minimizes the pairwise ranking loss from this paper.

Its abstract notes that TV sets are often shared by several users and that viewing data is typically collected and modelled per device, which hides individual tastes; it uses context to cope with this. That is relevant because the sweet.tv logs are per user_id and may mix household viewing, and it supports context (time-of-day) features.

Television Online Video (RecSysTV), held with ACM RecSys 2014, Foster City, CA, USA, Oct. 2014. [Online]. refs.why_relevant: The paper explains why linear-TV recommendation differs from VoD: programmes air at fixed times, so the catalog is dynamic (the new-item problem), consumption depends strongly on time context and channel preferences, and a viewer watches one channel at a time. It then extends standard recommenders with the current viewing context, tested on a large linear-TV dataset (abstract and introduction). This matches the sweet.tv setup, where the weeks 31-42 schedule is known.

CAVEATS
1. The Page et al. tech report: ilpubs.stanford.edu:8090/422/ is confirmed broken. It returns HTTP 200 with the body 'Failed to connect to database', and the PDF link returns HTTP 500. Use the Wayback URL given in the ref; the archived BibTeX gives Tech. Rep. 1999-66, Nov. 1999 (earlier number SIDL-WP-1999-0120). If a DOI-backed PageRank citation is preferred, use Brin & Page 1998 (A9 below).
2. Several sources could not be read directly:
   - dl.acm.org returns 403 to scripts and WebFetch, so ACM items rely on Crossref.
   - dblp is behind an anti-bot challenge (429).
   - link.springer.com is behind a JS challenge.
   - auai.org returns 503.
   Each was worked around: Springer data came from its citation export, LNCS volumes from library catalogs, and UAI and Stanford pages from Wayback snapshots.
3. Jeh & Widom: Crossref and OpenAlex give only the first page (271). The end page (279) is from Semantic Scholar.
4. LightGBM: cited without page numbers. The official NeurIPS BibTeX has an empty pages field and the OpenAlex/MAG page data conflict, so do not add the pages commonly seen elsewhere.
5. BPR: the UAI version has no DOI. The DOI given is the arXiv one, and the pages come from the arXiv report number UAI-P-2009-PG-452-461.
6. Ji et al.: Art. no. 75 comes from the arXiv journal reference, since Crossref has no article number.
7. Turrin et al. 2014: workshop paper with no proceedings, DOI or pages. It is confirmed by the official programme (archived) and the authors' PDF.
8. Campos et al. 2014 (A1): Crossref gives issue '1-2' but the Springer export says '1'. A1 follows Crossref.
9. Hu et al. 2008: only the abstract-level claim ('used ... within a recommender system for television shows') was verified. Do not quote dataset sizes for that paper from memory.
10. A guessed DOI 10.1145/1555349.1555363 turned out to be an unrelated paper. The correct DOI for Qiu et al. is 10.1145/1555349.1555381 (A19).

SUGGESTED 3-7 FOR RELATED WORK
- MF: hu2008 (plus rendle2009 if BPR is run).
- PPR: haveliwala2002 or jeh2003, plus gori2007.
- Association rules: agrawal1993 (or agrawal1994 for Apriori).
- Content-based: pazzani2007.
- TV: turrin2014 or aharon2015.
- Evaluation: ji2023 or meng2020.
- ke2017 and burges2010 only if a LightGBM ranker is used.
